plan.title: Three misses in a row: the honest day-3 check-in, then reworking the plan

context.text: Hey Sam! Ten pages of Dune on the couch at 7 tonight. Ready?
Sam, two nights slipped. Forget the ten: just open Dune tonight and read one page. What's getting in the way?

transcript.text: Hey Sam. You said you wanted to read Dune every day, and you committed to it. Is that still true? If you don't want to do this anymore, just tell me and that's totally fine. If you do, let's do it: ten pages on the couch at 7, starting tonight. And if the plan isn't working, we can change it to something that fits your life better. Let's just not give up on it.
honestly evenings are chaos with my new job, the plan isn't working

Totally fair, a new job will eat your evenings. Let's change the plan, not drop it. You've got a Dune streak worth getting back, and you did finish day 1. Is there a calmer pocket in your day, like morning before work or lunch, where 10 pages could fit?
mornings before work could work, like 7am

Locked in: 10 pages of Dune on the couch at 7 am, every day, with a photo of the page you stop on. I'll text you at 6:50 am to get you set up. You said you wanted this, and a morning slot gives you a real shot at it. Tomorrow we get the streak back.

Here's tomorrow's step: 10 pages of Dune on the couch at 7 am, about 20 minutes. Then send me a photo of the page you stop on. I'll text you at 6:50 am so you're ready. Mornings were your idea, and I think they'll work. Does that work for you?

checks.reason: Names today's step: ten pages of Dune on the couch at 7.
Says stopping is fine and frames the plan change as help, with no guilt or urgency.
Runs about four sentences, but the day-3 check-in is allowed to run longer and it has one question at the end.
Sincere and steady, with no overfamiliarity or emoji.
Plain words with no markdown or filler.
Two sentences plus one question at the end.
"Totally fair" and "not drop it" carry no guilt.
Names the new step: 10 pages of Dune on the couch at 7 am, with the photo proof.
Runs about four sentences with no question, and the first line is a list-like "Locked in:" fragment.
Gives what, where and when with proof, but leaves out the roughly 20-minute length already known.
States what, where, when, how long and proof.
Five sentences, though one question at the end.

conversation.reason: The day-3 check-in and timing were right, but the 7 am quiet-hours move was never offered, a 6:50 am text was promised inside quiet hours, and the settled step and time were re-asked in the last text.

grade.summary: ZOH's day-3 check-in was sincere, guilt-free and gave a real choice, and it reworked the plan around the tester's mornings instead of blaming them. It missed the quiet-hours offer for a 7 am step, promised a 6:50 am text inside quiet hours, and re-asked a step and time already agreed in its last text.
